hero.title: MSEI Lab
hero.description:
We investigate adaptive physical intelligence through tactile sensing, transferable learning, shared autonomy and embodiment across physical scales. Our research programmes connect robot manipulation, biomedical robotics, microrobotics and scientific experimentation.

Explore our research questions, published evidence, platforms and open research resources. The lab is directed by Dr Dandan Zhang, Assistant Professor at Imperial College London.

biographyParagraphs: MSEI Lab investigates how sensing, learning, control and embodiment can support precise, transferable physical manipulation.

Dr Dandan Zhang directs the laboratory in the Department of Bioengineering at Imperial College London. For her full biography, invited talks, teaching and individual academic service, visit her personal website.
hero.shortBio: The Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Laboratory, led by Dr Dandan Zhang at Imperial College London, researches adaptive physical intelligence across robotic scales.

data.title: Sensing and physical-state inference
data.intro: What can robots infer from touch and images?
data.description: We combine tactile sensor design, multimodal learning and microscopy-based perception to estimate contact, material properties and object state. Our studies connect visual–tactile fusion and sensor-side computation with cross-sensor benchmarking and data-efficient pose and depth estimation.

data.title: Transferable and data-efficient skill learning
data.intro: How can skills transfer with limited new data?
data.description: We develop learning methods that use structure in tasks, sensing and robot interaction to improve adaptation. Examples include one-shot imitation learning for pouring, multimodal diffusion policies for coordinated manipulation, and tactile skills transferred from simulation to physical robots.

data.title: Adaptive control and shared autonomy
data.intro: How should assistance adapt to the task and operator?
data.description: We study how robots and people can share control during precise manipulation. Context-aware assistance, adaptive motion scaling, digital twins and haptic feedback connect human intent with the physical demands of a task. We evaluate these methods in robotic surgery, teleoperation and magnetic micromanipulation.

data.title: Embodiment and actuation design
data.intro: How does physical design shape capability?
data.description: We investigate how materials, sensor geometry and actuation determine what a robot can sense and do. Our work includes inverse design of tactile elastomers, integrated tactile grippers, distributed optical-force control and modular magnetic robots. Physical design and control are developed together to enable new forms of manipulation.

researchoverview.description: Our goal is to develop robots that perceive physical interactions, adapt their behaviour and assist people in precise manipulation. We connect learning algorithms with the mechanics of sensors, tools and actuators, and evaluate these ideas through contact-rich tasks, medical robotics and scientific instrumentation. Explore the research themes and platforms and research publications.

opening.description:
We welcome enquiries from prospective researchers interested in tactile sensing, robot learning, shared autonomy, biomedical manipulation and optical or magnetic robotics. Relevant backgrounds include bioengineering, robotics, computer science, electrical engineering and related disciplines. Please see the Vacancies page and contact d.zhang17@imperial.ac.uk to discuss current opportunities.

Explore current scholarship schemes and applicant guidance on our opportunities page.

data.title: PhysLadder preprint
data.summary: Our collaborative PhysLadder preprint studies physical interaction in contact-rich manipulation using a matched simulation and real-world benchmark.

data.title: IROS 2026 workshop
data.summary: Dandan co-organised the IROS 2026 workshop Physical World Models for Scaling Embodied AI in Pittsburgh.

data.title: TR35 Asia Pacific 2026
data.summary: Dandan was recognised in MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 Asia Pacific 2026.

data.title: Magnetic microrobot fabrication in Artificial Life
data.summary: Our collaborative work on rapid parallel fabrication and magnetic control of diverse microrobotic structures has been published online in Artificial Life.

data.title: ECCV 2026 workshop
data.summary: Dandan co-organised the ECCV 2026 workshop Safe World Models for Trustworthy Embodied AI in Malmö.

data.title: ICRA 2026 sim-to-real microscopy
data.summary: Our ICRA 2026 paper on physics-informed sim-to-real data augmentation for micro-object pose estimation is available with open-source code.

data.title: Mag-VLA and optical digital twin preprints
data.summary: New preprints introduce Mag-VLA for bimanual magnetic microrobot manipulation and a digital twin for virtual visuo-haptic optical microrobot teleoperation.

data.title: Biomedical microrobotics review
data.summary: Our review of embodied cross-domain intelligence in biomedical microrobots has been published in Cyborg and Bionic Systems.

data.title: Micro-dexterity and Du-FreqNet preprints
data.summary: New preprints examine micro-dexterity in biological micromanipulation and introduce Du-FreqNet for depth-dependent optical microrobot microscopy image generation.

data.title: Bi-CAST and DexterousMag preprints
data.summary: New preprints explore adaptive shared control for bimanual magnetic micromanipulation and reconfigurable electromagnetic actuation with DexterousMag.

data.title: CBS 2025 optical depth estimation
data.summary: Our CBS 2025 paper on physics-informed optical microrobot depth estimation with adaptive grids is available with code.
